highlights.description: Recurring runbooks, such as a deploy, are run again from their first step, and a runbook's state says when each run began, finished or failed

added.description: `Runbook.Recurring` marks a runbook that is run again; `Log.Restart` begins a new run, `Log.Runs` records when each began, and a step's state comes from the current run's events while earlier runs stay as history

`StateOf` returns a `RunbookState`: each run's start, who began it and why, its last event, when it finished, its outcome (`not-started`, `in-progress`, `failed` or `finished`) and its steps by state, and when the runbook last finished
`Log.NextRunStart` and `Log.Current`: the earliest time a new run can begin, and the current run's events
`restart` and `state` commands; `state` prints text or `--format json`
On the HTML page, every link to another page is followed by an icon that opens it in a new tab; links within the page get none, and the icon needs no script

changed.description: The event log's schema adds `runs`, and the runbook's schema adds `recurring`; a log without runs is one run, so existing logs read as before

highlights.description: HTML pages are built from the runbook with templ components: full width, each step a section with its owner's badge, a copy button on every command, anchors shared with the Markdown page

changed.description: `Runbook.HTML` renders the runbook directly with templ components instead of converting its Markdown page: a full-width page, the phase summary as a table, each step a section with owner badges, its dependencies linked, its actions numbered with their commands escaped, and its credentials, done sentence and checks. Text fields are still Markdown, converted without raw HTML
`Style` uses the window's full width and adds step and badge styles

dependencies.description: Requires github.com/a-h/templ v0.3.1118; `go generate ./runbookspec` regenerates the components with that version

added.description: A copy button on every code block of the HTML page, for pasting a command into a terminal; `Script` is the script, for hosts that place the fragment in their own page

highlights.description: A runbook as data: phases of steps with owners, dependencies, actions and typed checks, validated, rendered as Markdown or HTML, recorded in an event log, and run step by step

added.description: The runbook model: phases, steps with an owner (operator, agent or both), dependencies, actions, a done sentence, checks and the credentials a step creates, with validation reporting every problem
An event log and each step's derived state: blocked, ready, in-progress, done or verified
Typed checks: dns, http, unreachable, command, and named checks a host registers in Go; checks only read, and report pass, fail or skip
Variables: declared {{name}} references in text, commands and checks, filled from flags, providers, the environment, or a command the variable declares

Guided runs: show each action with its variables filled, confirm and run commands without a shell, wait on a person's steps, stop at the first failure, record the step and run its checks; a new secret is generated in Go and piped to the program that stores it
A Markdown page with step and key links that never need anchors typed by hand, and a check for broken relative links
An HTML page: the Markdown page styled for light and dark themes, or its body for a host's own page, with raw HTML never passed through and angle-bracket placeholders shown

The Cobra commands a host tool mounts (validate, list, show, record, verify, run, doc with --html, schema), with a renameable events flag, and runbookspec, the command line over a runbook kept as JSON
JSON Schemas of a runbook and its event log, generated and embedded
